item.title: Patient experience data in regulatory and health technology assessment
item.content:encoded:
Wen-Hung Chen, AstraZeneca

Lori D. McLeod, RTI Health Solutions

Regulatory and health technology assessment bodies increasingly recognize the value of incorporating patient perspectives during product development and evaluation. Patient experience data encompass patient-reported outcomes, clinical outcome assessments, and patient preference information. However, there is inconsistency in how decision-makers collect, evaluate, and utilize these data, highlighting the need to understand different stakeholders' approaches to ensure patients' voices meaningfully influence healthcare decisions.

This collection invites submissions addressing how patient experience data—encompassing preferences, symptoms, and quality of life—can better inform regulatory and HTA processes. The collection welcomes original research, reviews, and discussion papers on recent developments in the field, as well as work exploring innovative applications such as artificial intelligence and digital health technologies in patient experience research.

Appel publié par Quality of Life Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Assessment of patient experience including preference, symptoms, and health-related quality of life
  • Patient experience data in regulatory submissions and health technology assessment decisions
  • Patient-reported outcomes and clinical outcome assessments
  • Patient preference information collection
  • Application of artificial intelligence and digital health technology in patient experience data research
  • Original research, reviews, and discussion papers on regulatory and HTA developments

Timeline

  • June 30, 2027: Submission deadline
